assembly_info.comments:
Background:
The Crithidia fasciculata (strain/isolate Cf-C1) was obtained from Dr. Larry Simpson, University of California, Los Angeles. Genomic DNA was prepared by CsCl/Ethidium bromide density gradient centrifugation to minimize the amount of kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA, and was provided by Drs. Natalia Akopyants, Lon-Fye Lye and Stephen Beverley, Washington University School of Medicine. The Crithidia fasciculata 14.0 assembly was assembled with Celera (v8.0) using 30X of PacBio long reads derived from an initial 130X coverage of PacBio reads, which were corrected by ECtools (v1.0) using the 13.3.5 reference assembly. The Celera assembly was further corrected using Quiver, and then ordered and oriented into pseudochromosomes by alignment to Leishmania major friedlin at the Myler lab. Finally, the assembly was gap-filled with PBJelly (v14.9.9), and error-corrected with icorn2. The final 14.0 assembly is made up of a total of 31 pseudochromosomes with an N50 pseudochromosome length of 1.3Mb and an N50 contig length of over 920Kb. The 427 unplaced contigs comprise nearly 8.7Mb of sequence. The assembled genome spans over 40Mb.
This work was supported by NIH grant AI29646 to SMB and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University.
For questions regarding this Crithidia fasciculata 14.0 assembly please contact Dr. Wesley Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@genome.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Crithidia fasciculata genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).
Source DNA can be obtained by mailing: Stephen M. Beverley, Ph.D. Marvin A. Brennecke Professor and Head of Molecular Microbiology Department of Molecular Microbiology Campus Box 8230 Washington University School of Medicine 660 S. Euclid Ave. St. Louis, MO 63110 USA
